About The Position

Riverside University Health System (RUHS) seeks candidates for an RUHS Compliance Program Manager position. This role supports the development, coordination, implementation, and oversight of RUHS corporate compliance programs and activities. The selected candidate will supervise support staff, ensure adherence to applicable regulations, and perform related duties as required. Current certification in Healthcare Privacy Compliance (CHPC)
is strongly preferred.

Key Responsibilities Include

Supporting compliance with federal, state, and county laws and regulations, including HITECH.
Providing subject matter expertise on medical privacy and information security.
Overseeing staff and managing program activities as assigned.
Assisting in achieving compliance goals and strategic objectives.

The RUHS Compliance Program Manager is a journey-level manager classification reporting to the RUHS/County Compliance and Privacy Officer. Incumbents are expected to perform complex and increasingly responsible work with minimal supervision, contributing to the design, execution, and monitoring of effective compliance programs. This position is distinct from the RUHS/County Compliance and Privacy Officer, which entails broader responsibilities in directing and managing regulatory compliance programs.

This class has been deemed eligible for the Performance Recognition Plan as set forth under Article 3, Section 311(C) of the County Management Resolution. Program eligibility requires employees to be in a leadership position, manage other employees or programs, and have significant influence on the achievement of organizational objectives.

Why RUHS Medical Center?

Riverside University Health System-Medical Center is nationally recognized for its innovative, progressive care and is considered one of the top employers in the region. The 439-bed Medical Center is a designated Stroke Center, Level I Trauma Center, and home to the only Pediatric ICU in the area.

For more information about RUHS Medical Center, please visit ruhealth.org .

Examples Of Essential Duties

Perform audits to assess compliance with various laws, regulations, policies, and standards such as those related to healthcare fraud, waste and abuse, billing and coding, clinical documentation, privacy and information security, research and ethics; maintain a system of reporting that provides timely and relevant information of all aspects of compliance issues.
Participate in appropriate level of response, develop corrective action plans and conduct compliance investigations while maintaining confidentiality of information reported, as appropriate.
Evaluate departmental continuous readiness to achieve compliance in the areas of healthcare privacy and security; assist in the development and implementation of privacy policies, procedures and breach notification as necessary.
Develop and implement policies and procedures for filing and investigation of complaints related to HIPAA/HITECH Privacy, Breach Notification Rules and related County guidelines and procedures.
Develop and monitor policies and procedures that establish standards for ensuring patient privacy protections, including by providing guidance to individual employees and departments on the HIPAA Privacy Rule, as appropriate.
Document and retain all complaints received as required by HIPAA/HITECH; establish and maintain a mechanism for tracking and reporting the investigation and resolving such complaints.
Develop and administer training for RUHS staff to promote awareness of compliance to regulatory standards.
Provide guidance and assistance to departments on a variety of privacy and compliance auditing, and internal control matters; document findings and prepare reports.
Supervise, assign, review, and evaluate the work performed by staff; direct the day-to-day operations of support staff.

Minimum Qualifications

Education:
Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree, preferably with a major in business administration, public administration, public health nursing, finance, accounting, or a closely related field to the assignment. (A master's degree from an accredited college or university in any of the aforementioned majors is preferred.) Possession of current Healthcare Privacy Compliance (CHPC) certification is preferred.

Experience:
Three years of professional, journey-level experience in healthcare compliance, which includes internal auditing experience and experience in the development and implementation of HIPAA and/or privacy compliance programs.

Knowledge of:
Information security; theory, principles and practices of general healthcare; governmental accounting, budgeting and auditing; HIPAA privacy and security rules and regulations; privacy laws, rules and regulations relating to information and security; federal, state and local codes, rules and regulations including healthcare fiscal operations; the methods of developing systems forms for various types of accounting records and reports; information systems and their application to accounting operations; the principles, methods and techniques of public administration, personnel and business office management; the principles and techniques of supervision.

Ability to:
Develop and implement compliance and auditing programs; apply legal and administrative compliance policies to hospital or health systems; analyze data, draw logical conclusions, conduct independent audits, reviews, and make evaluations to ensure compliance issues and concerns are appropriately evaluated, investigated and resolved; recommend effective courses of action; communicate effectively in oral and written form; establish and maintain effective working relationships; conduct independent systems analyses of complex business processes.

At Snap, the Technical Program Manager (TPM) is not a traditional project coordinator—this is a strategic, high-leverage leadership role designed for deep technical operators who thrive at the intersection of software engineering, data analytics, and program execution. TPMs at Snap are single-threaded owners of large-scale, high-stakes, and often ambiguous programs. They combine engineering depth with execution precision, earning visibility and trust across the company by driving outcomes that power the core of our products and infrastructure. Unlike industry-standard TPM roles, Snap TPMs are hands-on contributors who write Python notebooks, build dashboards and automation tools, and partner closely with engineering leaders to shape technical roadmaps, make architectural trade-offs, and drive the operating rhythm of the business. The most successful TPMs possess the ability to grasp new concepts quickly, navigate technical complexity, and adapt in fast-moving environments. This role is ideal for former engineers or data scientists who have evolved into program leaders without leaving their technical roots behind.

Our interview process reflects the technical rigor and strategic impact expected of TPMs at Snap. Unlike typical program management interviews, our process is designed to evaluate candidates’ ability to think like engineers and act like owners. Candidates begin with a technical screen with the hiring manager that dives into core program execution and engineering fundamentals. From there, The final stage is a virtual onsite, which includes a program leadership presentation and four 1:1 interviews with senior leaders across Snap. Throughout, we assess not only communication and collaboration skills but also technical fluency, first-principles thinking, and the ability to drive strategic outcomes in complex, ambiguous environments.

As a Technical Program Manager (TPM) at Snap, you will:

new_jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Description

Annapurna Labs designs the custom silicon that powers AWS's machine learning infrastructure, including the Trainium and Inferentia chip families. Our next-generation ML accelerator is a multi-die chiplet using advanced 2nm and 3nm process nodes with state-of-the-art packaging technology, and it is the most complex hardware program Amazon has undertaken. We are looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to own end-to-end program execution for this chip, from RTL freeze through tape-out and into production readiness.

This is not a status-reporting role. You will be the person who connects a sprawling set of engineering workstreams into a single coherent schedule, identifies the real critical path week to week, and drives the cross-functional decisions that keep the program on track. The program spans multiple concurrent silicon development efforts with significant interdependencies across engineering disciplines, external partners, and infrastructure.

Key job responsibilities

Own the integrated schedule and critical path analysis across multiple die tape-outs through engineering samples and production ramp. Understand dependency chains deeply enough to calculate the impact of any slip or pull-in, and update the timeline weekly with real data.

Drive the weekly chip status cadence by synthesizing inputs from RTL/DV, physical design, packaging, power, infrastructure, and post-silicon teams into a single view that tells leadership where we actually stand, including what is getting worse and what needs action.

Track verification convergence as a leading indicator by monitoring the progression from feature completion through RTL closure, bug trends, and regression pass rates by block. Recognize when convergence is stalling and drive the engineering response before downstream milestones are affected.

Manage the external design partner interface, owning the netlist delivery calendar, tracking your partner's physical design timeline, and negotiating schedule trades with a clear understanding of downstream cost.

Drive infrastructure readiness and external IP delivery by partnering with compute and EDA platform teams on capacity planning, and tracking third-party PHY, memory interface, and controller IP deliveries against consuming blocks to escalate gaps before they become tape-out critical.

A day in the life

You start your morning reviewing verification convergence dashboards and regression results, spotting a block where bug closure rates haven't flattened. You pull the DV lead and RTL owner into a quick sync to agree on a recovery plan before the weekly chip status review. In that review, you walk leadership through an updated critical path that reflects a netlist delivery shift from your external design partner, quantifying the downstream impact on tape-out timing. After lunch, you join an infrastructure capacity review to confirm that compute clusters can handle the regression load through freeze, then close out the day preparing an executive summary for an upcoming program milestone review.

About The Team

The Annapurna Labs ML Accelerator team builds the Trainium and Inferentia silicon that trains and serves machine learning models across AWS. We work at the intersection of chip architecture, physical design, verification, and infrastructure to deliver products that push the boundaries of performance and efficiency for our customers. Our team values people who bring strong technical judgment, clear communication, and a willingness to get into the details. If you want to shape how Amazon builds its most ambitious hardware and work alongside talented engineers solving real problems at scale, this is the role for you.

Basic Qualifications

10+ years of hands-on work managing complex technology projects experience
10+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
Deep working knowledge of the chip development lifecycle: RTL verification milestones, physical design convergence, DFT, and timing closure.
Experience managing programs with external design partners and IP vendors where you don't control the resources but own the outcome.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain integrated schedules with real dependency modeling — not just Gantt charts, but an understanding of which paths have float and which don't.
Strong technical communication skills: ability to present crisp status to VP-level audiences, distinguishing signal from noise, and framing decisions clearly.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with multi-die / chiplet / advanced packaging programs (2.5D/3D integration).
Familiarity with HBM integration, die-to-die interfaces, or high-speed serial subsystems.
Experience with leading-edge foundry nodes and their specific flow and schedule characteristics.
Background in ML accelerator or high-performance compute silicon.
Experience driving infrastructure capacity planning for large-scale chip development programs.

The Senior Preconstruction Project Manager – Energy Storage is responsible for leading the Energy Storage Preconstruction Group’s efforts with daily management, coordination, and successful completion of the energy storage project scope, budget, and schedule from notice of award to project mobilization. Additional responsibilities include managing project meetings, performing cost comparisons, updating project schedules, managing contract exhibits through execution, and strategic buyout negotiations as needed to maintain budget.

This job description reflects management's assignment of essential functions; it does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned

Able to perform all Preconstruction Project Manager job responsibilities
Maintain cost control ledger and job cost statements
Prepare billings and expedite payments
Set up and maintain all aspects of the CMiC system
Prepare bid packages and solicit and evaluate bids
Write project procedures
Review plans for completeness and accuracy
Supervise and train Preconstruction Project Engineers and clerical staff

Effectively manage project risk; evaluate probability and severity of risk events as they are identified / anticipated and prepare mitigation plans with project team operations management
Develop and maintain good relationship with Owner, Engineers, Vendors and Subcontractors; develop strategies and skills to build a strong partnership with the Owner, while still ensuring prompt owner notification of impacts and preservation of rights under the EPC

Minimum 3 years of Energy Storage Construction Experience.
Engineering, Construction Management or Architectural degree, or equivalent experience
Thorough understanding of plans and specifications
Field experience (5-8 years, Project Engineer or Assistant Superintendent)
Leadership ability – able to pull together team members from diverse backgrounds in a remote environment and organize them into a cohesive, high-performing project team

Strong computer skills with MS Office suite, as well as other industry-standard tools, such as Bluebeam Revu

Gwyneth Paltrow began goop in the fall of 2008 as a weekly newsletter. It has expanded into a beauty, fashion, and food business that’s also known for its products, curation, podcast, TV shows, live events, and retail stores.

About You

You're an executor. You take direction and turn it into action fast, with accuracy and follow-through. You live in Notion and Slack, you set up new tools with ease, and you run operations so smoothly that everyone knows what's happening, who owns it and when it's due.

Strong operational manager: you run the machine behind the business, including calendars, logistics, tools, vendors, budgets and follow-through
Systems builder: you learn new tools fast, set them up right the first time, and get people using them
Highly organized: you manage a high volume of parallel projects without dropping a thread
Skilled researcher: you gather information quickly and present it clearly
Thoughtful communicator, verbally and in writing: you're polished, considered and concise, you read the room, and you know how to communicate with a founder. Your updates, to-dos and summaries are clear, specific and easy to act on
Collaborative, with a good sense of humor: you stay steady and easy to work with under pressure
Trustworthy and discreet: you handle sensitive information with care

How You Operate

You communicate early and often; proactive updates are your default
You follow direction closely and ask the right questions when something is unclear
You're warm and direct
You understand that small details, done right, build long-term trust

About The Role

This role reports directly to goop's Founder & Co-CEO and is dedicated to the Founder's business. You'll work in close partnership with Co-CEO Moj Mahdara and the executive team, and you'll be a trusted, day-to-day point of contact for the Founder. Strategy and decisions are set by the two Co-CEOs; your job is to execute. You coordinate the projects and needs coming from both Co-CEOs and the executive team, and you make sure every action item is tracked, assigned and completed.

CALENDAR & LOGISTICS MANAGEMENT

Flag calendar conflicts, gaps and upcoming deadlines weeks ahead

PROJECT MANAGEMENT & EXECUTION

Execute projects led by the Co-CEOs: build the project plan in Notion, track milestones and owners, and drive every task to completion
Capture action items from executive meetings and make sure every one is tracked, assigned and closed
Keep a live view of all active projects showing what's in progress, what's at risk and what's blocked, and flag issues to the Co-CEOs early
Follow up with senior leaders and teams to keep deliverables on schedule

Route materials through the approval workflows set by the Co-CEOs, so items reach the Founder ready for review
Keep a master budget and vendor tracker for each project, including payment status and anything outstanding
Keep a current library of approved assets (bio, headshots, boilerplate, brand guidelines) so teams and partners always get the latest version

STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS DELIVERY

Project manage brand partnership deliverables once agreements are signed: timelines, assets, approvals and deadlines
Organize partner kickoff calls and keep a deliverables plan with owners, dates and approval status
Coordinate across internal teams and partner teams so deliverables ship on time and to spec
Keep partnership work-streams visible in Notion and Slack so the Co-CEOs always know their status

TOOLS & SYSTEMS SETUP

Set up new tools and AI apps selected by the Co-CEOs for the Founder and the executive team, including configuration, accounts, permissions and integrations
Onboard the Founder and executives into new systems with short training, simple guides and follow-up support until the tools are in daily use
Carry out tool migrations and consolidations (for example email platforms, inboxes and task systems) with minimal disruption
Connect tools so work flows between them automatically, for example meeting notes to Notion tasks, and Slack requests to tracked to-dos
Coordinate outside developers, consultants and IT partners working on systems, and keep their work on schedule
Work with IT and security to confirm new tools meet access and data-security standards before rollout

SLACK, NOTION & WORKSPACE MANAGEMENT

Organize projects in Slack using canvases, lists, pinned files and links, so every project has one clear home
Set up automated updates, summaries and reminders in Slack and Notion so the Co-CEOs and executive team get visibility without extra meetings
Build and maintain Notion databases, dashboards and templates for projects, to-dos and follow-ups
Administer the Slack and WhatsApp workspaces and keep them clean: channel and group structure, naming conventions, permissions, archiving and consistent project setup
Keep contact records and trackers accurate, deduplicated and consistently structured

RESEARCH & TREND REPORTS

Manage a pipeline of research requests from the Co-CEOs: log each request, track progress in Notion and deliver on deadline
Research and compile trend reports across wellness, beauty, fashion, consumer, culture and AI, following the briefs set by the Co-CEOs
Run quick research on companies, categories and markets as requests come in, and deliver clear, well-sourced summaries
Maintain a tagged, searchable research and trend library in Notion
Use AI research tools and agents to scan sources, summarize findings and track emerging signals

LOCATION, TRAVEL & HOURS

This is a remote role. You must be based in a North American time zone
You'll travel 8–10 times a year, for meetings, events and time with the team
You work on the Founder's schedule and are available during her working hours, including early mornings or late evenings when needed
Core hours align with Pacific or Eastern Time. The Founder travels regularly across time zones, so occasional flexibility is needed for time-sensitive travel, events and deadlines

Technical skills: Expert in Notion (calendars, databases, dashboards, templates, automations). Administrator-level experience with Slack (workspace setup, permissions, canvases, lists, workflows, channel management) and WhatsApp (business accounts, groups, access and security settings). Advanced user of Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini, and of Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides). Hands-on experience building workflows, AI agents and automations that connect these tools (e.g., Zapier, Notion automations, Slack workflows).
Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business required.
Skills: Exceptional written and verbal communication, with experience communicating directly with a founder or CEO. Exceptional organization, speed and follow-through, and experience working across time zones with global, cross-functional teams.
Based in North America and able to travel 8–10 times a year.

new_jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
About Us

We are the independent expert in assurance and risk management. Driven by our purpose, to safeguard life, property, and the environment, we empower our customers and their stakeholders with facts and reliable insights so that critical decisions can be made with confidence.

As a trusted voice for many of the world’s most successful organizations, we use our knowledge to advance safety and performance, set industry benchmarks, and inspire and invent solutions to tackle global transformations.

About The Role

Are you ready to shape the future of energy by leading high-impact M&A transactions across multiple energy technologies and helping grow strategic customer accounts?

Do you thrive at the intersection of technical expertise, commercial judgment, and strategic deal-making, helping investors make smarter decisions in a rapidly evolving energy market?

DNV Energy Systems North America is seeking a Senior Project Manager with a strong technical background in energy technologies (e.g. wind, solar, storage, electric-vehicle infrastructure, decarbonization, midstream infrastructure, thermal generation, data centers, or other emerging energy infrastructure), and/or practical experience with project financing for our Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A) Advisory Services team. The successful candidate will combine complex project delivery leadership with account growth, commercial ownership, and team capability development. Join us!

Our M&A team operates at the cutting edge of the energy industry providing technical due diligence and advisory services to diverse customers in the North American market and beyond, primarily in support of M&A transactions such as purchases, sales, divestments, and capital raises of projects and platforms. Our technical work contributes to the efficient functioning of the equity markets which are increasingly driving energy transactions in North America.

In this role, you will lead complex, high-value M&A engagements and serve as both a delivery leader and a senior relationship manager for selected strategic customers. You will provide senior-level project management and technical advisory services, exercise judgment across technical, commercial, and delivery trade-offs, grow key customer relationships, serve as Project Sponsor or senior reviewer for selected engagements, develop Project Managers (PMs) and Associate Project Managers (APMs), and translate experience into repeatable methods, tools, and best practices.

Ideally, this position can be based out of any of our current advisory offices including Seattle, WA; Portland, OR; San Diego or Oakland, CA; Austin, Houston, or Dallas, TX; Medford, MA; Arlington, VA; New York, NY; presenting a dynamic hybrid schedule where employees will typically spend three (3) days per week working from either a DNV office or client location/site

What You'll Do

Lead large, multi-discipline and multi-technology due diligence engagements, acting as the senior point of contact accountable for scope, schedule, budget, quality, customer confidence, and commercial outcomes. Identify technical risks and opportunities associated with potential investments, synthesize key findings, and clearly communicate their transaction implications to customers.
Leverage experience, expertise, and creative thought to deliver customer-centric technical analysis for energy and infrastructure projects. Typical scopes include evaluation of project risks and upside potential through:
Review of key project contracts describing interconnection, revenue, construction, and operations and maintenance;
Validation of technical inputs in project financial models including estimation and review of construction and operating costs;
Review of project designs and technologies;
Operational evaluations including site inspections and interviews (both on-site and virtual), and review of operating history and asset management approach; and
Industry benchmarking analyses and development stage project screening studies.

Provide senior oversight for due diligence execution, prioritizing QHSE considerations and ensuring a safe, healthy work environment across project teams.
Lead and coordinate technical reviews among internal specialists, including civil and electrical engineering, energy assessment, technology, transmission, permitting teams, and other DNV disciplines; establish clear accountabilities and resolve cross-discipline delivery issues.
Perform and/or provide senior review of due diligence including contract and financial model review as well as other technical analysis (e.g., technology review, contract review, energy assessment), with emphasis on the issues most material to the transaction.
Resolve technical issues in partnership with transaction stakeholders, including coordination of input on such issues from internal technical specialists, as necessary.
Lead the reporting and quality assurance process, including writing, editing, reviewing, approving, and synthesizing inputs from technical disciplines into clear, technical due diligence reports aligned with customer’s commercial needs.
Lead customer dialogues to understand their needs. Develop winning proposals for scopes of services related to due diligence work, including creative tailoring and sequencing of work to meet budget and timeline requirements. Identify opportunities for innovation and refinement to meet the needs of an evolving marketplace.
Support customers through transaction execution, investment committee decisions, financing, and closing, as applicable
Lead continuous improvement efforts for the M&A team, such as tool development, process refinement, training, and lessons learned activities.
Adhere to the DNV system for quality management, including liaising with QHSE leadership on developing procedures, instructions, guidelines, and checklists in order to ensure quality of services produced by the M&A team.
Mentor Project Managers and Associate Project Managers through project-based coaching, review, and knowledge sharing; provide input to Team Leads on development needs, project assignments, and readiness for increasingly complex responsibilities.

What we offer

Generous paid time off (vacation, sick days, company holidays, personal days)
Multiple Medical and Dental benefit plans to choose from, Vision benefits
Spending accounts – FSA, Dependent Care, Commuter Benefits, company-seeded HSA
Employer-paid, therapist-led, virtual care services through Talkspace
401(k) with company match
Company provided life insurance, short-term, and long-term disability benefits
Education reimbursement program
Flexible work schedule with hybrid opportunities
Charitable Matched Giving and Volunteer Rewards through our Impact Program
Volunteer time off (VTO) paid by the company Career advancement opportunities
Benefits vary based on position, tenure, location, and employee election**

For California, Washington, New York, Washington, D.C., Illinois, and Maryland: “DNV provides a reasonable range of compensation for this role. The actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors, including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and specific location. For the states of California, Washington, New York, Washington, D.C., Illinois, and Maryland only, the starting pay range for this role is $135,000.00 - $180,000.00.”

DNV is a proud equal-opportunity employer committed to building an inclusive and diverse workforce. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, or business need, without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

DNV is committed to ensuring equal employment opportunity, including providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. US applicants with a physical or mental disability who require reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or hiring process may contact the North America Recruitment Department (hrrecruitment.northamerica@dnv.com). Information received relating to accommodation will be addressed confidentially.

For more information

https://www.eeoc.gov/know-your-rights-workplace-discrimination-illegal

About You

What is Required

Bachelor’s degree from accredited four-year university in a relevant field to include engineering, science, thermal generation, renewable energy, finance, business or other related areas.
Typically, 7+ years of applicable technical and project management experience in the thermal, solar, wind, storage, and/or energy infrastructure in North America. Battery energy storage systems (BESS) experience is preferred but not required.
Knowledge of the energy project lifecycle and associated items which may include project contracts (EPC, equipment procurement, interconnection, PPA, etc.), technology and design, energy production assessments and performance, financial modeling and economics (CapEx and OpEx), operations and performance, transmission/curtailment considerations, and common technical risks.
Demonstrated willingness to adopt, test, and improve digital and AI-enabled delivery tools, including using project experience to help translate workflows into scalable methods, templates, and quality controls.
Demonstrated ability to balance technical, commercial, schedule, and transaction priorities while maintaining a focus on issues most material to investment decisions.
Demonstrated experience owning project financial performance, including budget, margin, invoicing, scope control, and change orders.
Demonstrated experience leading proposals, shaping scopes for complex transactions, and contributing to account or pipeline growth.
Experience mentoring project managers or technical professionals and providing quality or sponsor-level oversight across multiple engagements.
Proficiency in MS Office Suite.
Ability to travel domestically and internationally to customer offices and sites, other office locations, and conferences, up to approximately 15% of the time.
Excellent verbal and written communications skills in English.
We conduct pre-employment drug and background screening

*Immigration-related employment benefits, for example visa sponsorship, are not available for this position*

Personal Qualifications And Skills

Leadership skills, strong team mindset, and the ability to collaborate, motivate and lead by way of example.
Commitment to customer centricity and demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships with customers.
Ability to work effectively and professionally with diverse customers and colleagues.
Ability to distinguish material transaction issues from ordinary technical observations.
Flexibility, resiliency and adaptability within a dynamic team environment.
Continuous improvement mindset and enthusiasm for leveraging digital and AI-enabled tools to improve project delivery, quality, and efficiency.
Drive to learn, and collaboratively identify opportunities for improvements to process, tools, and offerings.
Strong technical and organizational skills.

We are seeking a dedicated IT Project Manager/Scrum Master who can perform project management and business analysis. This position would join NDOT’s Information Technology Project Portfolio Management Office (PPMO) team in helping to manage IT projects from initiation to closure.
Under general direction, this position would be responsible for planning, directing and coordinating project management activities of designated project(s) ensuring that the goals and objectives of the project(s) are accomplished within the prescribed timeframe and requirements. Set deadlines, assign responsibilities and monitor and summarize progress of project. Prepare reports for project portfolio and upper management regarding status of project.
The successful candidate will work directly with clients to ensure deliverables fall within the applicable scope and budget. Perform a variety of tasks. Lead and direct the work of others. A wide degree of creativity and latitude are expected. Will report to the Lead IT Project Manager.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Strong soft skills with a distinctive ability to empower, motivate and influence others without authority or a direct reporting relationship.
Develop requirement specifications, business cases, functional specifications, process models and state transition models.
Define project scope, goals and deliverables that support business goals in collaboration with senior management and stakeholders.
Perform gap analysis to compare solutions against stakeholder requirement. Conduct vendor product evaluations.
Enhancing the capabilities and effectiveness of NDOT, by ensuring that proposed solutions are properly understood and appropriately exploited.
Proven working experience in project management.
Excellent client-facing and internal communication skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Solid organizational skills including attention to detail and multitasking skills
Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office
Proven experience in project management.
Ability to lead project teams of various sizes and see them through to completion
Strong understanding of formal project management methodologies such as Project Management Institute (PMI)
Experience as an IT project manager or ERP project manager
Leading process to complete project charter and obtain necessary approvals
Creating and publishing project documents to include project scope, project schedule, business requirements, risk assessment and response, and time estimates
Determining resources required to accomplish project objectives.
Conducting or participating in stakeholder meetings
Creating and executing plans for communication, change control, quality and risk control, and specific coordination of activities.
Oversee execution of project tasks, monitoring performance and solving project slippage and/or constraints in timely manner
Managing stakeholder expectations, project risks and solving problems
Controlling project scope and changes, schedule, and status reporting
Facilitate closeout activities like lessons learned and customer feedback
Extremely detail oriented
Perform analysis and document process flows.
Understand and perform QA/QC functions as well as potentially lead others in QA/QC activities.
Capture business requirements and assist with design and development.
Experience with Azure DevOps to create product backlogs, user stories & tasks
Must be able to perform Process Flow Analysis of existing systems/applications.
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Candidate must be able to work onsite and remotely when required
Regular and reliable attendance is required
Experience supporting Department of Transportation / Highway Safety / Traffic Safety / Financial systems.

QUALIFICATIONS
Required:
Qualified applicants will have a Bachelor's degree or technical degree in Computer Science/Software Development/Project Management (or equivalent combination of education and minimum 5+ year’s Project Management experience).
Must have minimum 2+ years of experience in managing projects/software development utilizing Agile SDLC.
Minimum 5 years project management experience

Experience with all aspects of project management.
Experience with Agile development utilizing SCRUM.
Data Analysis
Experience working with Developers and end users is a plus.
Project Management certification desired, but not required.
Perform or assist with testing as needed.
Experience with Web Services and Windows Services.
Experience using Microsoft SQL Server
Experience with CICS.
Experience handling multiple projects.
Written and Verbal communication skills
MS Office
Integration planning and strategy
Presentation skills
NDOT web applications are built in MVC pattern with MSF C#.NET, HTML, JavaScript, CSS and XML which interact with the Department's Information Systems.

Compensation & Location

Location:
Greensboro, NC (onsite 4 days/week)
Pay Range:
$41.00 – $48.00 per hour (based on experience, geographic region, and internal equity)
Schedule:
Full-time, contract; long-term opportunity through December 2028
Travel:
Approximately 5%
Benefits:
Health, Vision, Dental, Life Insurance, 401k, Continuing and on-demand education

📍 Must be willing to work in Greensboro, NC

✅ Sponsorship is available for this role

‼️ ONLY W2 – NO CORP to CORP – NO 3rd Parties

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced IT Project Manager to lead the planning and execution of enterprise technology initiatives involving business and IT stakeholders, SAP functional and technical resources, infrastructure, security, testing teams, and external vendors.
This role will oversee projects throughout the full delivery lifecycle, including requirements, design coordination, system integration testing (SIT), user acceptance testing (UAT), defect management, deployment readiness, cutover, go-live, hypercare, and transition to support.

Key Responsibilities

• Project planning, scope, schedule, resources, milestones, RAID management, governance, status reporting, stakeholder engagement, vendor coordination, quality, and change control
• Manage the delivery lifecycle including requirements, design coordination, SIT, UAT, defect management, readiness, cutover, go-live, hypercare, and transition to support
• Lead project planning and execution for PS&P initiatives by defining scope, objectives, deliverables, milestones, schedules, dependencies, resource needs, and governance expectations with business and IT stakeholders
• Coordinate cross-functional project teams, SAP functional and technical resources, infrastructure, security, testing teams, external vendors, and business subject-matter experts to maintain alignment and delivery accountability
• Maintain integrated project plans and track actions, risks, issues, assumptions, dependencies, decisions, and change requests; escalate items requiring leadership direction and follow through to closure
• Prepare clear project status reports covering accomplishments, upcoming milestones, schedule health, risks, issues, dependencies, decisions, and required management actions
• Facilitate project meetings, requirements workshops, design reviews, testing checkpoints, readiness reviews, cutover planning sessions, and post-launch stabilization meetings; document decisions, owners, and due dates
• Coordinate SIT and UAT planning, test readiness, execution progress, defect triage, business sign-off, deployment readiness, cutover, go-live, hypercare, and transition to support
• Apply change-control and quality-management practices to validate scope changes, assess business and technical impacts, coordinate approvals, and protect committed delivery outcomes

What You'll Be Working On

• PS&P initiatives
• Enterprise IT project planning and execution
• SAP functional and technical workstreams
• Cross-functional business and IT initiatives
• Requirements and design coordination
• System Integration Testing (SIT)
• User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
• Defect management and business sign-off
• Deployment readiness and cutover planning
• Go-live, hypercare, and transition to support
• Project governance and status reporting
• Risk, issue, assumption, dependency, decision, and change management
• Business, technical, and vendor stakeholder coordination

Required Skills & Experience

• 10+ years of experience in IT project management, program delivery, or enterprise technology implementations

Works with management and stakeholders to align priorities and goals using technical know-how in a fundamental engineering area or technical domain. Technical Management and Execution - Technical Management:

– Leverages technical knowledge to identify risks, manage scope, estimate program timelines, request feasibility, testing requirements, and determine appropriate resources.

– Ensures that product or service delivery meets the third party, security, export, and accessibility compliance requirements.

– Drives rapid response to security escalations, coordinating across teams and communicating to executives to assess risk, determine mitigation strategies, and align and execute optimal proposed path to resolution.

– Forecasts program demands and resourcing to identify risks and ensure that goals are achievable.

– Leads the development and implementation of evolving processes to ensure that organizational SLAs are met.

Technical Management and Execution - Technical Strategy and Execution:

– Utilizes technical knowledge to identify, track, and manage program dependencies and risks.

– Supports rapid response to escalations, coordinating within team and communicating to senior team members to assess risk, determine mitigation strategies, and execute the optimal proposed path to resolution.

– Supports planning by identifying dependencies and risks.

– Develops delivery standards and guidelines in alignment with Oracle best practices.

– Identifies and quantifies opportunities for process automations and advocates for prioritization.

– Contributes to incident management efforts and identifies opportunities to improve processes, as applicable.

Program Oversight - Strategy and Decision-Making:

– Aligns priorities with customers, service, and stakeholder teams through regular reporting to senior leadership.

– Establishes scope and milestones for each program, aligning to the broader program plan and company strategies and goals.

– Assists in defining key performance indicators (KPIs) and measurement methods for program performance against established goals (e.g., scope, timelines, deliverable quality).

– Builds, maintains, and executes a clear communication strategy of objectives to partners and customers, influencing decision-making regarding best practices for Oracle systems.

Program Oversight - Program and Operations Management:

– Manages both technical and non-technical programs and complex, cross-organizational programs impacting products and business.

– Guides the work of program staff (e.g., development, release management, customer success) while providing technical support and direction on removing barriers, including risks and issues in workflows.

– Maintains comprehensive program documentation (e.g., status reports, program plans) and documents risks and issues.

– Ensures attention to detail in program management from planning to execution and reporting.

– Leads regular program status meetings and keeps teams and leadership informed.

– Leads initiatives within the team to improve operational efficiency and enhance adherence to service level agreements (SLAs) and productivity targets.

– Ensures ownership and accountability for forecasting program demands, funding, and resourcing.

– Guides the deployment of change management for programs, such as priority, scope, scheduling, or requirement changes.

Program Oversight - Risk Management:

– Manages highly complex issues, bottlenecks and/or risks, escalating issues when appropriate.

– Conducts comprehensive assessments of costs, benefits, and return on investment (ROI) to inform decision-making and risk mitigation strategies.

– Manages critical issues while making trade-offs between business needs and technical constraints.

– Removes blockers for the program and identifies new technical and resource options to efficiently deliver solutions and drive adoption.

Process Efficiency - Process Optimization:

– Leads program improvement, implementing best practices and driving cross-team process optimizations to improve processes.

– Organizes and develops program objectives and workflows, while testing and deploying cross-functional solutions to address critical business problems.

– Collaborates with management to initiate and maintain processes and procedures that guide and assist teams in reaching their goals.

Process Efficiency - Continuous Improvement:

– Leads efforts to integrate continuous improvement within programs, driving insights across many workstreams to generate recommendations that deliver operational efficiencies.

– Develops and standardizes data-driven decision-making frameworks, ensuring insights drive efficiencies.

– Identifies and addresses gaps to facilitate business-critical improvements to the solution's availability and reliability.

– Iterates processes based on feedback and KPIs, analyzing results through retrospectives.

– Defines requirements and configurations of existing and new development tools, where applicable.

Collaboration and Program Leadership - Cross Functional Collaboration:

– Facilitates collaboration across multiple teams, driving discussions that align priorities and program goals.

– Leads medium-scale efforts to optimize processes, identifying and implementing solutions that enhance team efficiency.

– Delivers program updates, risks, and opportunities to managers and leadership, influencing decision-making.

– Develops relationships with key stakeholders, ensuring their perspectives are integrated into program planning and execution.

Collaboration and Program Leadership - Program Leadership:

– Leads programs to continuously improve organizational efficiency.

– Provides technical direction and mentorship to cross-functional teams.

– Influences and guides change at all levels of the group from initiation through delivery.

– Ensures that the program team and other stakeholders are aligned with the program goals and motivated, identifying and addressing conflicts and issues.

Data and Analysis:

– Creates and automates reporting, partnering with development teams to continue improving reports, dashboards, forecasts, and models to help manage program execution.

– Utilizes data to solve moderately complex problems impacting the success of the program(s), including adherence to SLAs.

– Conducts analysis on a small number of data sources with moderate complexity, which may include competitive analysis, trend analysis, and KPI analysis, to drive data-informed decisions to support the program goals, presenting findings with immediate teams stakeholders.

Stakeholder Engagement:

– Acts as a liaison with or between stakeholder teams, driving effective collaboration for customer success within Oracle commitments.

– Manages relationships with internal and external stakeholders to align program priorities and commitments.

– Identifies and documents stakeholder needs and works cross-functionally to implement solutions that enhance satisfaction.

– Identifies risks to customer satisfaction and advocates for improvements or mitigation.

– Assesses risks to customer satisfaction and evaluates mitigation efforts, providing solutions to the immediate team and related teams to ensure alignment on resolving these risks.

– Helps balance team priorities and Oracle commitments to ensure optimal coverage and response to key customer needs, minimizing risks to the program.

Core Responsibilities

Planning & Execution:

– Manages and coordinates moderately complex tasks, monitoring timelines and deliverables to ensure timely completion and adherence to requirements for a moderately sized project or initiative. Efficiently delegates, monitors, and prioritizes work across multiple projects, providing technical oversight and adjusting plans to address shifts in resources or timelines.

Leverages understanding of business leaders, stakeholders, and/or customers to ensure proposed solutions meet their needs. Supports inclusivity by actively seeking and listening to diverse perspectives, ensuring others feel heard and respected.

Proactively seeks and leverages ongoing feedback and training to improve skills. Coaches and mentors junior team members, fostering continuous learning and knowledge sharing within and across teams.

Solicits feedback from others on ideas for alternative approaches and methods for continued improvement.

new_jobs.description:
Our Story & Purpose:

We’re Vancity, a member-owned credit union built on the principles of inclusion and social justice. Since 1946, our relentless commitment to these values has helped us challenge the status quo and break down barriers. We’ve made bold commitments to become net-zero by 2040 across all mortgages and loans, and we’re actively pursuing strategies in Indigenous banking and financial resilience for our members.   
As the largest private sector Living Wage Employer in Canada, we’re proud to be consistently recognized as one of the country’s Top Employers. If you’re ready to join our team of 2,700 diverse individuals, access competitive rewards and benefits, and be part of a greater movement - apply today!  

Your Role in Supporting Our Members:

As a Co-ops & Local Economies Program Manager
, you will work closely with senior leadership to advance Vancity’s Co-ops & Local Economies Strategy by creating the conditions for members, businesses, and communities to thrive through stronger local economies, community ownership, and co-operative development. You will build strategic partnerships, generate sector insights, develop innovative initiatives, and identify opportunities that help businesses start, grow, modernize, transition ownership, and keep economic value rooted in community. This role is ideal for a strategic and community-minded professional who is passionate about co-operative development, local economic resilience, partnership building, and creating measurable economic impact.   
This is a Full-time, Permanent
role based at our Vancity head office
and will report directly to the Director, Co-Ops and Local Economy
. While this position provides a hybrid work arrangement, you will be expected to be on-site for events and business demands.  

How You'll Make an Impact:

Supporting the development and delivery of programs and initiatives that strengthen co-operatives, small businesses, and local economic ecosystems  

Developing tools, frameworks, and partnership approaches that help internal teams activate strategy at scale through innovative models and impact capital  

Building and managing relationships with co-operatives, sector associations, community organizations, economic development partners, and industry stakeholders  

Identifying and activating partnerships that support co-operative growth, local enterprise, community ownership, and wealth recirculation  

Connecting internal teams and external partners to advance collaborative initiatives and community-based opportunities  

Participating in industry convenings, working groups, and stakeholder forums to identify trends, build relationships, and generate new opportunities  

Advancing opportunities that connect co-operative development, community ownership, economic resilience, and local enterprise with Vancity products and services  

Conducting research on co-operative development, local economic trends, community wealth-building models, and inclusive business practices  

Translating research, stakeholder insights, and market intelligence into practical recommendations, business cases, and financing pathways  

Developing compelling storytelling, impact reporting, presentations, and communications materials that demonstrate outcomes and strengthen awareness  

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Community Development, Public Policy, Commerce, Urban Studies, Social Enterprise, or a related discipline  

5+ years of experience in program management, community economic development, social finance, co-operative development, partnership management, or a related field  

Demonstrated experience developing and delivering programs, partnerships, or initiatives that create economic or community impact  

Experience building and managing relationships across non-profit organizations, co-operatives, government agencies, financial institutions, and community partners  

Strong research, analytical, and strategic thinking skills with the ability to synthesize complex information into actionable recommendations  

Experience developing business cases, presentations, reports, and briefing materials for senior leadership and external stakeholders  

Excellent stakeholder engagement, facilitation, communication, and relationship management skills  

Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and initiatives simultaneously  

Extra Skills That Set You Apart:

Experience working within co-operative sectors, social enterprise ecosystems, or community wealth-building initiatives  

Experience supporting impact investing, impact capital, economic development, or inclusive business growth programs  

Knowledge of small business development, ownership transition, community ownership models, or local economic resilience strategies  

You’ll Thrive Here If You Are:

Impact-Oriented
- You are motivated by creating lasting economic and community benefits.  

Relationship-Focused
- You build meaningful partnerships and bring diverse stakeholders together around common goals.  

Strategic
- You connect emerging opportunities with broader organizational and community objectives.  

Collaborative
- You thrive working across sectors, disciplines, and stakeholder groups.  

Curious
- You actively seek innovative ideas, insights, and approaches that strengthen local economies and community wealth.  

We value lived experience, so if you are interested in this role, we encourage you to apply even if you feel your skills don't perfectly align with those listed.  

What You’ll Earn:

This role offers a salary range of $108,500 to $140,500 per annum
. The base pay offered may vary depending on factors such as relevant qualifications, skills, previous experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards package, employees may also be eligible for our annual incentive program, subject to program eligibility requirements.  

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

A career at Vancity is more than just a job, you’re joining a tradition of change-makers who are creating lasting change for our communities. Beyond base pay, we offer a comprehensive total rewards package to ensure our employees are empowered to thrive:  
Living Wage Employer
: We’re the largest private-sector Living Wage Employer in Canada and consistently ranked among Canada’s Top Employers  

Customizable Benefits
: Permanent employees receive flexible benefit packages that can be tailored annually to meet evolving needs  

Generous Vacation
: New employees start with 3-4 weeks of vacation per year, with additional days earned over time  

Extra Stat Holidays
: In addition to BC’s 11 statutory holidays, we offer 2 extra days, plus care days for personal or family illness  

Immediate Health Coverage

Defined Benefit Pension

Any information you choose to share will be stored securely and used only for recruitment and career development connected to this initiative, in line with the BC Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA).

We are committed to an inclusive, barrier-free and accessible recruitment experience for all candidates. 합류하게 될 팀에 대해 알려드려요

Global UX Research Program Manager는 토스의 글로벌 서비스를 준비하는 팀에서 함께 일해요.
토스는 '누구에게나 쉽고 상식적인 금융'을 한국을 넘어 더 많은 나라의 사용자에게 전하기 위한 준비를 하고 있어요. 해외 시장과 유저에 대한 깊은 이해도를 바탕으로 각 국가의 문화와 맥락에 자연스럽게 녹아드는 서비스를 만드는 목표를 가지고 있어요.
글로벌 시장에서 성공하기 위해서는 현지 시장과 유저를 깊이 이해하는 것이 중요해요. 이를 위해 글로벌 유저의 데이터와 인사이트가 지속적으로 쌓일 수 있는 리서치 인프라를 설계하고, 글로벌 유저 리서치의 중장기 방향을 만들어가고 있어요.

합류하면 함께 할 업무에요

효율적인 리서치 실행을 위해 글로벌 리서치 프로세스를 최적화하고, 비효율적인 영역을 찾아 개선하는 업무를 담당해요.
인사이트가 활용될 수 있도록 공유 프로세스를 구축하고, 조직에서 쉽게 접근하고 활용할 수 있는 환경을 마련해요.
조직 내 리서치 문화 정착과 역량 강화를 위해, 리서치 방법론과 실무 적용 방안을 학습할 수 있는 교육 프로그램을 만들고 운영해요.
해당 포지션은 사용자 리크루팅과 운영을 포함하여, 내부 리서치 프로세스를 최적화하고 리서치 툴과 프로그램 기획 및 개선을 주도하는 역할을 해요.

이런 분과 함께하고 싶어요

문제를 스스로 정의하고, 조직 내 새로운 프로세스를 만들거나 개선한 경험이 필요해요. 여러 이해관계 속에서 우선순위를 정하고 리소스를 나눌 수 있어야 해요.
해외 파트너사와 이메일로 소통하고, 글로벌 고객과 인터뷰 일정을 잡을 때 필요한 영어 역량이 필요해요.

Job Description

OCI Strategic Customer Engineering is seeking an experienced Principal Program Manager with technical interests to lead large-scale, cross-functional initiatives that drive strategic outcomes across Oracle Cloud Infrastructure which span highly technical and business-centric delivery. This role is ideal for an accomplished program leader who thrives in highly technical environments, excels at navigating ambiguity, and has a proven ability to deliver complex programs from inception through execution.

You are a results-oriented leader who drives execution—not just coordination. You possess strong judgment, exceptional ownership, and a bias for action. You dig deep to master a space and understand it full. You build trusted partnerships across engineering, product management, operations, customer success, and executive leadership to align teams around common objectives and deliver meaningful business and customer outcomes.

As a Principal Program Manager, you will lead programs that span multiple OCI organizations, helping teams prioritize, execute, and deliver initiatives that improve operational excellence, customer success, and strategic business objectives. The work is highly visible, fast-paced, and requires balancing technical complexity with operational and business complexity with organizational alignment.

Basic Qualifications

BS degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field
7+ years of experience in Program Management, Software Engineering, Product Management, or related technical leadership roles
Experience leading large-scale, cross-functional programs across multiple engineering organizations
Strong understanding of cloud technologies, distributed systems, and software development lifecycles
Demonstrated ability to drive execution in complex, fast-moving environments with multiple stakeholders
Experience developing program plans, tracking execution, managing dependencies, and mitigating risks
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach to decision making
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting to executive leadership
Proven ability to influence without direct authority and build consensus across diverse organizations
Strong customer focus with the ability to balance technical priorities and business objectives
Preferred Qualifications
MS degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field
10+ years of experience in Program Management or engineering leadership
Experience working with cloud-native architectures and large-scale distributed systems
Experience managing strategic customer programs or enterprise cloud initiatives
Familiarity with Agile, Scrum, and modern software development methodologies
Experience working directly with executive stakeholders and large enterprise customers

Responsibilities

RESPONSIBILITIES

Program Leadership

Lead complex, cross-functional programs from planning through execution and successful delivery.
Define program goals, milestones, success metrics, and execution plans that align with organizational priorities.
Coordinate engineering, product management, operations, and customer success teams to deliver high-impact initiatives.
Drive program governance, status reporting, executive communications, and stakeholder alignment.
Identify program risks, dependencies, and execution challenges while developing proactive mitigation strategies.
Establish scalable program management processes and mechanisms that improve organizational execution.
Manage competing priorities and ensure successful delivery across multiple concurrent initiatives.
Break down complex technical initiatives into manageable workstreams with clear ownership and accountability.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Build strong partnerships across OCI engineering, product, operations, support, and executive leadership teams.
Drive alignment across organizations to ensure successful execution of strategic initiatives.
Facilitate technical and business discussions that enable informed decision-making and accelerate delivery.
Communicate program status, risks, and recommendations to stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Foster collaboration across geographically distributed teams and organizations.

Operational Excellence

Identify opportunities to improve processes, remove operational bottlenecks, and increase organizational efficiency.
Develop repeatable mechanisms, dashboards, and reporting processes that improve program visibility and execution.
Lead post-launch reviews and continuous improvement efforts to enhance program delivery.
Support strategic planning activities, roadmap execution, and organizational prioritization.
Help teams scale effectively by implementing best practices for program management and operational excellence.

Customer & Business Impact

Partner with internal and external stakeholders to understand customer priorities and translate them into executable programs.
Drive initiatives that improve customer experience, operational efficiency, and business outcomes.
Balance customer needs, technical constraints, and organizational priorities while making informed tradeoff decisions.
Ensure programs deliver measurable value for both OCI and its strategic customers.

What Success Looks Like

Strategic initiatives are delivered on time, with high quality and strong cross-functional alignment.
Engineering, product, and business teams have clear visibility into priorities, risks, and execution progress.
Operational processes scale efficiently as the organization grows.
Executive stakeholders have confidence in program execution through consistent communication and measurable outcomes.
OCI Strategic Customer Engineering successfully delivers initiatives that improve customer experience, operational excellence, and business performance.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager - Body
new_jobs.description:
About Rivian

Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.

As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.

Role Summary

Rivian's Body Manufacturing Engineering (ME) team designs, launches, and continuously optimizes world-class manufacturing systems to produce safe, high-quality vehicles at scale. As a Senior Technical Program Manager, you will lead cross-functional scope execution across joining, assembly, tooling, and simulation workstreams—translating program commitments into technical readiness and proactive risk mitigation.

Body Manufacturing Engineering oversees joining processes, assembly line equipment, tooling strategy, and advanced simulation across product updates, DFM studies, and program management lifecycles.

We are seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to serve as the connective tissue across joining, assembly equipment, tooling, and simulation disciplines—aligning key deliverables (cost, timing, quality, mass, and CAPEX/ED&D investment) with structured execution and proactive risk management. This role is located at our Normal, IL facility and reports directly to a Sr. Manager, Manufacturing Engineering.

Responsibilities

Drive the integrated program schedule for Body Manufacturing Engineering (joining, assembly, tool design, simulation, and DFM) from initial concept through SOSP and steady-state production.
Align cross-functional teams—including Design Engineering, Supply Chain, CAPEX/Finance, Facilities, and Plant Operations—to ensure equipment, tooling, and process readiness adhere to Rivian Development Process gate milestones.
Identify and mitigate program risks regarding cost, timing, quality, mass, and tooling budget through structured gate reviews, design evaluations, and issue resolution frameworks.
Translate advanced DFM studies and simulation insights into actionable design and process decisions, maintaining continuous feedback loops between simulation models, tool design, and line-side execution.
Manage technical engineering change requests, tooling modifications, and line trials for running product updates to minimize impact on production.
Oversee tooling vendors and equipment suppliers through schedule management, buy-off, installation, and commissioning milestones.
Establish and maintain standard program management practices (reporting cadences, dashboards, escalation paths) to translate complex engineering topics into executive-level communications.
Support prototype, pilot, and pre-production build events to ensure Body ME deliverables and launch readiness are actively managed.
Leverage data and AI tools to create auto-generated reports and dashboards to reduce administrative burden while focusing efforts on resolving real problems.
Responsible for driving escalation topics and focusing escalation pathways on problem resolution and productive outcomes.
Embody the "Rivian Compass" values across all workstreams and team interactions.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, or related technical field); Advanced degree preferred.
4+ years of experience in automotive manufacturing engineering, technical program management, or body-in-white (BIW) development, with direct involvement in joining, assembly systems, or tooling programs.
Strong technical understanding of body-in-white manufacturing processes is preferred. Knowledge of joining methods (resistance spot welding, SPR, structural adhesive, laser welding), assembly tooling design/build lifecycles, DFM principles, and simulation analysis (stamping feasibility, tolerance stack-up, line accessibility) are preferred.
Demonstrated ability to lead multi-workstream programs in a fast-paced, matrixed environment—converting ambiguity into defined project scopes, key deliverables, and actionable timelines.
Proficiency with program management tools (e.g., MS Project, Smartsheet, Jira) and experience building program tracking structures from the ground up.
Proven track record collaborating with CAPEX, Supply Chain, Facilities, and Manufacturing teams to deliver tooling and equipment on time and within budget.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, applying a first-principles, systems-thinking approach to problem-solving and executive-level presentations.

Pay Disclosure

The salary range for this role is $111,600-$138,700 for Illinois based applicants . This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.

The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.

We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. You may also have the opportunity to participate in Rivian’s 401(k) Plan and Employee Stock Purchase Program if you meet certain eligibility requirements. Full-time employee coverage is effective on their first day of employment. Part-time employee coverage is effective the first of the month following 90 days of employment. More information about benefits is available at rivianbenefits.com.

You can apply for this role through careers.rivian.com (or through internal-careers-rivian.icims.com if you are a current employee). This job is not expected to be closed any sooner than 10/1/2026.

Equal Opportunity

Rivian is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Rivian is committed to ensuring that our hiring process is accessible for persons with disabilities. If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at candidateaccommodations@rivian.com.

Candidate Data Privacy and Technology

Rivian may collect, use and disclose your personal information or personal data (within the meaning of the applicable data protection laws) when you apply for employment and/or participate in our recruitment processes (“Candidate Personal Data”). This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. Rivian may use your Candidate Personal Data for the purposes of (i) tracking interactions with our recruiting system; (ii) carrying out, analyzing and improving our application and recruitment process, including assessing you and your application and conducting employment, background and reference checks; (iii) establishing an employment relationship or entering into an employment contract with you; (iv) complying with our legal, regulatory and corporate governance obligations; (v) recordkeeping; (vi) ensuring network and information security and preventing fraud; and (vii) as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law.

Rivian may share your Candidate Personal Data with (i) internal personnel who have a need to know such information in order to perform their duties, including individuals on our People Team, Finance, Legal, and the team(s) with the position(s) for which you are applying; (ii) Rivian affiliates; and (iii) Rivian’s service providers, including providers of background checks, staffing services, and cloud services.

new_jobs.title: Compliance Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Department / Seat Name: Compliance

Location: Remote (Role is open to only U.S.-based, U.S.-citizen-only)

Salary: $105,000-$145,000

Type: W2; Full-Time

Role Summary

The Compliance Program Manager owns the full lifecycle of compliance frameworks across the

organization, from regulatory monitoring and internal program readiness through to the

productization and launch of new service offerings. This role is the single accountable owner

for knowing what is changing in the regulatory and framework landscape, determining what the

organization must do about it internally, and converting qualifying frameworks into repeatable,

sellable, deliverable service lines.

This is a hybrid compliance and product role. Approximately half the seat is program

management: tracking framework requirements, owning internal compliance obligations,

maintaining authorization and accreditation readiness, and driving remediation to closure. The

other half is product management: business case development, scoping, methodology design,

pricing input, enablement, and launch coordination for new offerings.

The role is not a people management position but carries cross-functional accountability

across PMO, TAC, Sales, RFP, Marketing, and Finance.

Role Purpose

To ensure the organization is never surprised by a compliance change, never out of

compliance with the frameworks and authorizations it operates under, and never late to

market with a new offering that the changing landscape creates demand for.

Core Responsibilities

Compliance Program Ownership
Own the organization-wide compliance framework calendar, tracking rule changes,

standard revisions, program updates, and authorization requirements across all

frameworks the company operates under or delivers against

Maintain a current obligations register mapping each external requirement to an internal

owner, control, artifact, and evidence location

Drive internal readiness for new and renewing authorizations, accreditations, and

program approvals, including document production, gap closure, and submission

coordination

Coordinate internal audits, surveillance activities, and external assessment cycles,

including scheduling, evidence collection, corrective action tracking, and closure

verification

Track and drive corrective actions, nonconformities, and findings to documented

closure with defined owners and due dates

Monitor regulatory and standards bodies for changes affecting the organization's

authorizations, delivery methodologies, or service eligibility, and issue timely impact

analyses to leadership

Maintain the compliance obligations documentation set, ensuring version control,

currency, and traceability

Serve as the internal subject matter expert on framework requirements, providing

authoritative interpretation to delivery, sales, and leadership teams

Escalate impartiality, independence, conflict of interest, and eligibility questions to the

appropriate authority rather than resolving them unilaterally

Productization and Offering Ownership

Evaluate emerging and revised frameworks for market opportunity, producing a written

business case covering demand signal, competitive landscape, required capability,

margin profile, and go/no-go recommendation

Own the end-to-end productization of approved offerings, including scope definition,

deliverable set, methodology, work breakdown structure, level of effort model, and

quality gates

Partner with Finance and Sales leadership to develop pricing, rate card entries, and

margin targets for new offerings

Build and maintain the delivery artifact set for each offering, document templates,

evidence requirements, and reporting formats

Partner with TAC and delivery leadership to define staffing requirements, required

credentials, and technical readiness for each new offering

Develop and deliver enablement materials for Sales, RFP, and delivery teams, including

positioning, qualification criteria, and scoping guidance

Own the launch plan and post-launch review for each new offering
Maintain the offering portfolio, identifying offerings that should be revised, repriced,

consolidated, or retired

Partner with Marketing on messaging accuracy and technical claim review for all

compliance-related content

These are tracked weekly or monthly via the Scorecard:

Percentage of tracked frameworks with a current obligations mapping
Open corrective actions past due
Average days to close a corrective action
Authorization and accreditation milestones met on schedule
Regulatory change impact analyses issued within the defined SLA
Number of framework evaluations completed
Number of offerings launched per quarter against plan
Days from go decision to first sellable offering
Days from go decision to first delivered engagement
Revenue attributable to offerings launched in the trailing four quarters
Enablement completion rate across Sales and delivery teams for each launched offering
Internal audit and surveillance findings attributable to program management gaps

Right Mindset & Cultural Fit

This role requires someone who consistently demonstrates:

You read primary sources rather than relying on summaries, vendor blogs, or

secondhand interpretation

You are comfortable owning an outcome without owning the people who produce it
You bring a recommendation, not just a problem, and you can defend it with evidence
You are equally comfortable in a requirements document and in a pricing model
You move quickly on market opportunity without cutting corners on compliance

obligations

You escalate independence and impartiality questions early rather than working around

them

You write clearly enough that a salesperson, a project manager, and an assessor can all

act on the same document

You align with RSI's Core Values and commitment to quality

Misalignment Indicators

This seat is considered vacant or at risk if the person:

Learns about a framework or regulatory change after the market or a client does
Allows corrective actions, findings, or obligations to sit open without escalation
Produces offerings that Sales cannot sell or that delivery cannot execute profitably
Treats productization as documentation work rather than as owning a commercial

outcome

Defers framework interpretation questions upward instead of developing authoritative

command of the requirements

Launches offerings without pricing, staffing, delivery templates, and enablement in

place

Resolves impartiality or independence questions unilaterally rather than routing them to

the appropriate authority

Cannot establish credibility with delivery leads, assessors, or client-facing teams
